scope: One chunk decoded at several budgets
title: Detail against components read
description: One chunk stored as a single hologram decodes 98.4 percent correct at the full budget, and the hologram read shrinks as the budget falls.
claim: One 16 by 16 chunk stored as a single hologram decodes 98.4 percent of its cells correctly at the full budget of 8,192 components and 131,072 bytes. Reading fewer components is smaller and fuzzier: 67.1 percent at 1,568 components, and 19.5 percent at 24, which takes 384 bytes.

headline.label: of cells decoded correctly with all 8,192 components
less hologram read at 24 components than at the full budget

method.workload: A chunk of a fixed procedural world is built at full fidelity. For each component budget it is decoded as a colour field and checked cell by cell against the stored block (Chunk.Accuracy). The hologram size is the number of bytes CapacityProbe reports for that budget.
engines: HoloVoxel Chunk.DecodeField at ten component budgets
method.verification: Accuracy is the share of surface cells whose strongest decoded block equals the block that was stored.
method.statistic: Accuracy is one measurement of one chunk.
method.memory: Hologram size is sixteen bytes per component read.
method.tie: Eight blocks are possible, so a random guess is right 12.5 percent of the time.

losses: Accuracy is low at small budgets by design: 19.5 percent at 24 components, against 12.5 percent for a random guess. A far read is a soft blend, not a smaller copy of the near one.
limits: One chunk of one world. Terrain with other block mixes will score differently.
Accuracy is measured at full resolution for each budget. The scene on the product page also coarsens the grid with distance, which this table does not measure.
